extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies preparing NEPA documents (EISs), cooperating agencies, and public commenters/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_short: NEPA EIS commenting and decision rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural criteria for public commenting on Environmental Impact Statements (EISs), interagency dispute resolution, Records of Decision (RODs), mitigation (including enforceability and monitoring), and agency responses under the CEQ NEPA regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional integrity of NEPA documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must ensure the professional integrity, including scientific integrity, of the discussion and analysis in their NEPA documents (not just EISs) and make use of reliable data and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision moved to part 1506 (§1506.6). Applies broadly to quality and reliability of data and analysis across NEPA documents; intended to address confusion and align with NEPA statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to comment on specific submitted alternatives not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies need not specially invite comment on submitted alternatives, information, analyses, or their summaries (deletion of 40 CFR 1503.1(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ deleted the requirement because agencies already invite comment on all sections of draft EISs (including appendices); inviting comment on one specific section is unnecessary and redundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of comments — 'as specific as possible'
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should be 'as specific as possible'; CEQ strikes the 2020-language requiring comments to be as detailed 'as necessary to meaningfully participate and fully inform the agency.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal intended to avoid imposing an ambiguous and burdensome standard that could require technical expertise or detailed analyses from lay commenters and could chill participation or drive unnecessary litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenters not required to describe data/sources/methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters do not need to describe their data, sources, or methodologies; only where possible should the public include citations, proposed changes to the EIS, or describe supporting data/methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ clarifies that such information is helpful when readily available but should not be construed to place an unreasonable burden on commenters or imply they must collect/produce supporting information.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to couch issues in economic/employment terms
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ deletes language suggesting comments must cover economic and employment impacts or 'other impacts affecting the quality of the human environment' in economic terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEPA requires analysis of potential effects on the human environment, but commenters need not frame issues economically; deletion avoids implying commenters must address these impacts in economic terms while preserving agencies' obligations under §1501.2(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of exhaustion-related timing requirement for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ removes the exhaustion provision (paragraph (b) of 40 CFR 1503.3 (2020)) that could constrain when commenters must file issues; agencies retain discretion to consider special/unique circumstances for comments outside standard time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change intended to avoid tying NEPA comment timing to administrative-law exhaustion doctrines and to preserve opportunities for public engagement (scoping, draft EIS comment period) while reducing litigation-focused timing constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating agencies identify additional information needed generally (not just 'site-specific')
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperating agencies must identify additional information needed to address significant effects; CEQ struck 'site-specific' to clarify that identification applies generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change enhances efficiency by ensuring cooperating agencies request needed information to fully comment on EISs and avoid delays; no substantive comments were received on this change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating agencies must specify statutory authority when recommending mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: A cooperating agency with jurisdiction by law shall specify mitigation measures and cite its applicable statutory authority when recommending mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ retained (and strengthened) this requirement to clarify the duty to identify mitigation measures and the legal authority for them; CEQ encourages early identification (no later than review of draft EIS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must respond to comments (shall respond)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must respond to comments on an EIS ('shall' respond) and may do so individually, in groups, or a combination thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstating 'shall' removes ambiguity introduced in 2020 that could be read to make responding voluntary; agencies retain flexibility in the manner of response to promote efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to summarize/respond to similar or non-substantive comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies have discretion to summarize and respond to comments of a similar nature, or decline to respond to comments the agency determines provide no substantive information applicable to the EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined to define 'substantive comments' (to avoid unnecessary restriction). The list of response means is illustrative, not mandatory; agencies should ensure they respond to individual comments or groups as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errata usage and final EIS completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency uses an errata sheet, the agency must publish the entire final EIS including the errata sheet, a copy of the draft EIS, and the comments with their responses so the public can access the complete analysis in one place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change reflects typical electronic submission practice and clarifies intent to ensure public access to the full record; final EIS 'includes' the errata sheet and copy of the draft statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage early interagency dispute resolution (informal, discretionary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are encouraged (but not required) to engage early with one another to resolve interagency disagreements concerning proposed major Federal actions before referring disputes to CEQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision codifies longstanding practice of collaboration and CEQ's role as convener/mediator; discretionary, flexible, non-binding approach intended to promote early resolution and efficient environmental review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required when requesting CEQ informal dispute resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting CEQ engage in informal dispute resolution, an agency must provide CEQ with a summary of the proposed action, information on the disputed issues, and agency points of contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision codifies what CEQ needs to mediate effectively; designed for informal, early dispute resolution distinct from formal referral procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEQ response options to informal dispute resolution requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a request for informal dispute resolution, CEQ may request additional information, convene discussions, make recommendations, or decline the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ's options are flexible and non-binding; intended to allow CEQ to assist agencies in resolving disputes without supplanting agency authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for referrals include non-exclusive 'other appropriate considerations'
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria list for referrals (moved into §1504.3(a)) is not exclusive; CEQ added an 'other appropriate considerations' factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies CEQ's discretion in deciding whether to accept a referral and prevents overly rigid application of enumerated factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for other interested persons to provide views on referrals; public meetings allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ revised rules to allow 'other interested persons' (not just applicants) to provide views on referrals and clarifies CEQ may obtain additional views and information including through public meetings or hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expands participation in CEQ's referral consideration and confirms public meetings/hearings are permissible tools for gathering views.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROD must identify alternatives considered and the environmentally preferable alternative(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Record of Decision, an agency must identify the alternatives it considered in reaching its decision and specify one or more environmentally preferable alternatives (which must be among the alternatives included in the EIS: proposed action, no action, or reasonable alternatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ clarifies the environmentally preferable alternative must be one of the alternatives analyzed; CEQ declined to require agencies to explicitly state whether they selected the environmentally preferable alternative or to require explanation if they did not (to avoid being overly prescriptive).

rubrics_metrics.name: ROD discussion of mitigation: 'mitigate' and 'adopted all practicable means'
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ revised language to use 'mitigate' (instead of 'avoid or minimize') and requires agencies to discuss generally whether they have 'adopted all practicable means' to mitigate environmental harms in the selected alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies need not discuss mitigation on an impact-category-by-impact-category basis; requirement is to discuss mitigation generally and explain reasons for not adopting practicable means where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceability requirement when agencies rely on mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency's ROD incorporates mitigation and the EIS analysis of reasonably foreseeable effects is based on implementation of that mitigation, the mitigation must be enforceable by the lead, joint lead, or cooperating agency, and the agency must identify the authority for that enforceable mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revised text to clarify when enforceability is required; examples of enforceable mitigation include permit conditions or agreements. This is to prevent agencies from basing analyses on mitigation they cannot ensure will occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and compliance plan required for enforceable mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must prepare a monitoring and compliance plan consistent with §1505.3 when mitigation is enforceable and relied upon in the analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ requires a monitoring and compliance plan to ensure assumptions about mitigation in the NEPA analysis are correct; discussion of monitoring is integrated with §1505.3 provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to include enforceable mitigation in every NEPA decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations do not mandate enforceable mitigation in every decision; agencies may approve proposals with unmitigated adverse effects or include unenforceable mitigation so long as the agency does not rely on the assumed effectiveness of that mitigation in its analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If agency treats unmitigated effects as 'reasonably foreseeable' and analyzes them, the rule does not require mitigation be made enforceable or authority identified. The focus is on not basing analyses on mitigation the agency cannot be reasonably sure will occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies should not base NEPA analyses on mitigation they lack authority to carry out
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must avoid relying in their NEPA analyses on mitigation measures that they lack statutory authority to require or ensure will occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ emphasizes integration with other statutory processes and transparency; requirement to identify the authority for enforceable mitigation helps align NEPA with other statutory frameworks rather than duplicate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of ROD certification that agency considered all submitted alternatives/info
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ struck the ROD certification paragraph (previously requiring explicit certification that the decision maker considered all submitted alternatives, information, and analyses) as redundant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ concluded the decision maker's signature and the ROD discussion already serve to verify consideration; removal also ties to elimination of exhaustion provisions and avoids creating unnecessary compliance burden or implication that other parts of the record were not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to incorporate mitigation for environmental justice impacts (§1505.3(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ adds and finalizes a provision encouraging lead and cooperating agencies to, where appropriate, incorporate mitigation measures addressing significant adverse human health and environmental effects that disproportionately and adversely affect communities with environmental justice concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision is intended to highlight and encourage consideration of environmental justice in mitigation and decisionmaking; CEQ received mixed comments but finalized the provision with edits.
